subject: Data retention exception request – FinServ trial / next steps
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@finserv.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: PrivacyOps <privacy@finserv.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Data handling requirements (PII / retention)

Thanks for the demo earlier – appreciate the walkthrough. A quick recap from our side and the asks we discussed:

- Use case: in-product LLM assistant that will receive customer PII (names, account IDs, partial SSNs).
- Hard requirement: zero persistent storage of request/response payloads (0-retention) for production. Logs for debugging must be minimized and redacted.
- Data residency: all processing must be in our US region (we discussed a dedicated instance).
- Audit & attestation: we need evidence (SOC 2 / DPA) and a contractual clause guaranteeing no retention of PII beyond the session.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) run a Dedicated environment with 0-retention for payloads, 2) provide a technical approach for redaction or on-the-fly tokenization, and 3) share DPA/SOC2 docs for legal review?

Sara from legal is looped on this thread for contract language.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Green
Head of Platform Security, FinServ Bank
alex.green@finserv.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@finserv.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, PrivacyOps <privacy@finserv.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data handling requirements (PII / retention)

Thanks Alex – great questions and thanks for laying these out. Recap and proposed options below. Copying Marissa (CS lead) and Camila (security/legal partner) to detail technical and contract options.

Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can run a Dedicated instance in a US region and restrict processing to that environment.
- For 0-retention of request/response payloads we have two paths:
  1) Dedicated/Private deployment with logging disabled and request/response not written to persistent storage (recommended).
  2) Hosted with redaction proxy (less ideal for strict 0-retention).

Tradeoffs: Dedicated/Private gives us the cleanest contractual guarantees but requires provisioning (lead time ~2–3 weeks for Pilot). We can offer a timeboxed trial (30–90 days) with 0-retention configs enforced and monthly attestation.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share our latest DPA and SOC2 report (attached).
2) Marissa will outline the exact technical changes required to disable retention and what telemetry – if any – remains for availability/debugging.
3) Camila will propose the specific DPA clause language / exception for the retention schedule and confirm DocuSign flow.
4) If that sounds right, we can schedule a short legal/ops call this week to confirm scope and timelines.

Attachments: DPA_redwood_v3.pdf, SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf

Rafael
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-19T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data handling requirements (PII / retention)

Alex – quick technical note on options and what we need from you to scope the pilot:

Options we can implement in Dedicated/Private:
- Disable request/response persistence: payloads are processed in-memory and not written to disk. KV/cache can be rotated to ephemeral only.
- Redaction pipeline: a pre-processing proxy that removes PII fields based on regex or a custom schema (we can supply a lightweight template).
- Reduced telemetry: we can turn off application-level request logging; infra/health metrics remain but can be aggregated without payloads.

What we need from FinServ to finalize the proposal:
- Expected request volume (RPS / monthly tokens) and average prompt/response sizes.
- Example payloads (sanitized) so we can confirm redaction rules.
- Confirmation of which headers (e.g., Authorization, X-User-Email) must be redacted or never stored.

Attached: retention_proposal_finserv.xlsx – includes a recommended retention schedule and estimated cost delta for Dedicated with 0-retention.

If acceptable, we can provision a Pilot namespace with the 0-retention config and run a 30-day trial.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finserv.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Alex Green <alex.green@finserv.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T08:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data handling requirements (PII / retention)

Rafael – thanks for the fast follow-up. A couple of legal items we want to confirm before proceeding:

1) Contract language: we need an explicit clause in the DPA that Redwood will not retain request/response payloads containing customer PII beyond the session and will not use payload data for training.
2) Auditability: we require a monthly attestation that the environment was configured as promised and a one-time access to redact logs for the pilot period.
3) SLA: we need clarification on whether disabling request logging affects incident response and what the fallback plan is if we detect production issues.

Please include Camila or your security lead to draft the DPA amendment and confirm the attestation wording.

Regards,
Sara Patel
Senior Counsel, FinServ Bank
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finserv.com>, Alex Green <alex.green@finserv.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data handling requirements (PII / retention)

Sara / Alex – thanks, and appreciate the clarity. Below is suggested contract and technical language we can add to the DPA for the pilot and a proposed implementation plan.

Suggested DPA clause (pilot):
"Redwood will not persist request or response payloads that contain Customer PII in the Dedicated environment provisioned to Customer for the duration of the Pilot. Any telemetry or logs retained for operational purposes will be redacted and aggregated such that individual request/response payloads are not reconstructable. Redwood will not use Customer payloads to train models."

Implementation plan (pilot):
- Provision Dedicated namespace in US region with logging disabled for application-level request payloads.
- Enable preprocessing redaction proxy; provide FinServ with redaction rules and run test vectors.
- Monthly attestation report (PDF) signed by Redwood security confirming config.
- Pilot duration: 30 days (can extend to 90 days subject to agreement).
- DocuSign flow for DPA amendment: link provided after acceptance.

Next steps: Rafael / Marissa – can you confirm FinServ's expected RPS and whether you want 30 or 90 days for the initial pilot? Once we have that I’ll prepare the DPA amendment and DocuSign envelope.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
